Richie Laryea climbing all-time Canada caps list, hopes to play 2030 World Cup

  • Benedict Rhodes
  • @btfr17
  • Share Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Bluesky Share on Reddit Share via email
  • September 16, 2026
  • •
  • 5 min read
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:51
Instaread

Richie Laryea has the rare distinction of being one of just 13 Canadian men to have played at two World Cups. As the new cycle begins toward the 2030 tournament, he’s hoping to make it to a third.

Laryea was a key part of both the 2022 squad that qualified Canada for the first time in 36 years, and this summer’s team that had another rare opportunity to play a World Cup on home soil. Still one of the most important players for Toronto FC and Canada, there is absolutely still a world in 2030 where Laryea finds himself on the plane.

He will be 35 then, but says that as long as he can still play at a good level he’ll be fighting for the chance to wear the maple leaf.

“Like I always do, take it one step at a time,” Laryea said to reporters including Waking The Red on Wednesday. “It’s this camp and then the following camp, take it like that. I see myself as a competitor, I always want to compete, I always want to hold myself to the highest regard and to compete at the highest level. I would hope when 2030 comes around, I’m still feeling really good, still competing really well and in contention to being part of the team again for another World Cup.”

He added that getting a third chance to play on the biggest international stage would be “incredible” and thinks “that’s what everyone that went to this past World Cup should have on their mind as well.”

“If I feel the way I feel right now, I have no doubt I’ll be in a good spot,” he concluded.

Laryea first broke into the national team under John Herdman, during the first of now three stints with Toronto FC back in 2019. He has since been a fixture for Canada, making 80 appearances over the past seven years, including starting all five games this summer with Alphonso Davies out injured.

His flexibility to play at left-back, right-back, centrally, in midfield or further up the pitch on either flank makes him a valuable asset for both Marsch and TFC boss Robin Fraser. An MLS All-Star for the first time this year as well, he is still performing at the highest level in North America.

As Canada looks to end a 26-year trophy drought on the men’s side since the 2000 Gold Cup, Laryea is going to be a key factor in the national team for at least the next couple of years with Nations League in a few months, plus the 2027 Gold Cup and potentially 2028 Copa America if Canada gets invited again. If there’s anyone you want competing against the South American footballing dark arts, it’s Laryea.

One camp at a time is the message from the Toronto native, and that starts next week.

Laryea has been brought into camp by Marsch for a BMO Field friendly against Chile on Sept. 26, which will be followed by a trip to Montreal on Oct. 3 to play Peru, then St. Paul, MN to take on the United States. All three games will be intense, especially the one against the Americans, as they usually are in any sport.

He is one cap shy of moving into ninth-place all-time for the men’s national team, passing Milan Borjan (80) and equalling Dwayne De Rosario (81). If he plays in all three games this window he’ll also pass Randy Samuel’s 82, with Jonathan David also at 82.

Laryea will likely reach 100 if he goes the full World Cup cycle. Cyle Larin (94) and Jonathan Osorio (92) — who is not in this camp due to injury but will continue to be considered by Jesse Marsch — are the closest players to reaching Atiba Hutchinson’s record 104 men’s caps.
